sanskrit: dṛṣṭiś cātīndriyā rājan dūrāc chravaṇam eva ca paracittasya vijñānam atītānāgatasya ca
english: And by his grace, O king, I have gained sight that transcends the senses, hearing across great distances, knowledge of others' thoughts, and awareness of things past and yet to come.

sanskrit: vyutthitotpattivijñānam ākāśe ca gatiḥ sadā śastrair asaṅgo yuddheṣu varadānān mahātmanaḥ
english: Knowledge of births that have arisen out of due course, the power to move ever through the sky, and immunity from weapons in battle — all this from the boon of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: śṛṇu me vistareṇedaṃ vicitraṃ paramādbhutam bhāratānāṃ mahad yuddhaṃ yathābhūl lomaharṣaṇam
english: Hear from me, then, in full this wondrous tale, most marvelous and hair-raising — how the great war of the Bhāratas came to pass.

sanskrit: teṣv anīkeṣu yat teṣu vyūḍheṣu ca vidhānataḥ duryodhano mahārāja duḥśāsanam athābravīt
english: When those armies had been drawn up in array according to rule, Duryodhana, O great king, then spoke to Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: duḥśāsana rathās tūrṇaṃ yujyantāṃ bhīṣmarakṣiṇaḥ anīkāni ca sarvāṇi śīghraṃ tvam anucodaya
english: "Duḥśāsana, let the chariots that guard Bhīṣma be yoked at once, and urge on all the divisions with all speed.

sanskrit: ayaṃ mā samanuprāpto varṣapūgābhicintitaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ sasainyānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca samāgamaḥ
english: This clash of the Pāṇḍavas with their hosts and of the Kurus, brooded upon through many long years, has at last come upon me.

sanskrit: nātaḥ kāryatamaṃ manye raṇe bhīṣmasya rakṣaṇāt hanyād gupto hy asau pārthān somakāṃś ca sasṛñjayān
english: I deem no task in battle more urgent than the guarding of Bhīṣma; for, well protected, he will slay the Pārthas, the Somakas, and the Sṛñjayas with them.

sanskrit: abravīc ca viśuddhātmā nāhaṃ hanyāṃ śikhaṇḍinam śrūyate strī hy asau pūrvaṃ tasmād varjyo raṇe mama
english: And he of pure heart has said, 'I will not slay Śikhaṇḍin; for it is told that he was once a woman, and so he must be spared by me in battle.'

sanskrit: tasmād bhīṣmo rakṣitavyo viśeṣeṇeti me matiḥ śikhaṇḍino vadhe yattāḥ sarve tiṣṭhantu māmakāḥ
english: Therefore Bhīṣma must be guarded with especial care — such is my judgment; let all my men stand ready, bent on the slaying of Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: tathā prācyāḥ pratīcyāś ca dākṣiṇātyottarāpathāḥ sarvaśastrāstrakuśalās te rakṣantu pitāmaham
english: Let the warriors of the East and the West, of the South and of the Northern road, skilled in every weapon and missile, guard the grandsire.

sanskrit: arakṣyamāṇaṃ hi vṛko hanyāt siṃhaṃ mahābalam mā siṃhaṃ jambukeneva ghātayāmaḥ śikhaṇḍinā
english: For unguarded, even a wolf may slay a lion of mighty strength; let us not have our lion slain by Śikhaṇḍin as though by a mere jackal.

sanskrit: vāmaṃ cakraṃ yudhāmanyur uttamaujāś ca dakṣiṇam goptārau phalgunasyaitau phalguno 'pi śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: Yudhāmanyu guards Phalguna's left wheel and Uttamaujas his right — these two are Phalguna's protectors, and Phalguna himself protects Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyamāṇaḥ pārthena bhīṣmeṇa ca vivarjitaḥ yathā na hanyād gāṅgeyaṃ duḥśāsana tathā kuru
english: So act, Duḥśāsana, that Śikhaṇḍin — guarded by Pārtha and shunned by Bhīṣma — may not be able to slay the son of Gaṅgā."

sanskrit: tato rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ śabdaḥ samabhavan mahān krośatāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ yujyatāṃ yujyatām iti
english: Then, when the night had passed into dawn, a great clamor arose from the kings crying out, "Yoke them! Yoke them!"

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaiḥ siṃhanādaiś ca bhārata hayaheṣitaśabdaiś ca rathanemisvanais tathā
english: With the blare of conches and kettledrums, with lion-roars, O Bhārata, with the neighing of horses and the rumble of chariot wheels,

sanskrit: gajānāṃ bṛṃhatāṃ caiva yodhānāṃ cābhigarjatām kṣveḍitāsphoṭitotkruṣṭais tumulaṃ sarvato 'bhavat
english: with the trumpeting of elephants and the roaring of warriors, with shouts and the slapping of arms and battle cries — a tumult rose up on every side.

sanskrit: udatiṣṭhan mahārāja sarvaṃ yuktam aśeṣataḥ sūryodaye mahat sainyaṃ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ tava rājendra putrāṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ tathaiva ca
english: At sunrise, O great king, the whole vast host of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava armies arose, fully arrayed without exception — the forces of your sons, O lord of kings, and of the Pāṇḍavas alike.

sanskrit: tatra nāgā rathāś caiva jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtāḥ vibhrājamānā dṛśyante meghā iva savidyutaḥ
english: There the elephants and chariots, adorned with gold, were seen gleaming like clouds shot through with lightning.

sanskrit: rathānīkāny adṛśyanta nagarāṇīva bhūriśaḥ atīva śuśubhe tatra pitā te pūrṇacandravat
english: The masses of chariots looked like cities beyond number; and there your father shone exceedingly, like the full moon.

sanskrit: dhanurbhir ṛṣṭibhiḥ khaḍgair gadābhiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ yodhāḥ praharaṇaiḥ śubhraiḥ sveṣv anīkeṣv avasthitāḥ
english: With bows, spears, and swords, with maces, lances, and javelins, with gleaming weapons of war, the warriors stood firm each in his own division.

sanskrit: gajā rathāḥ padātāś ca turagāś ca viśāṃ pate vyatiṣṭhan vāgurākārāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Elephants, chariots, foot soldiers, and horses, O lord of peoples, stood ranged like an outspread net, in their hundreds and their thousands.

sanskrit: dhvajā bahuvidhākārā vyadṛśyanta samucchritāḥ sveṣāṃ caiva pareṣāṃ ca dyutimantaḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Banners of many fashions were seen raised aloft, radiant by the thousand, both of one's own side and of the foe.

sanskrit: kāñcanā maṇicitrāṅgā jvalanta iva pāvakāḥ arciṣmanto vyarocanta dhvajā rājñāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: Golden, their staffs bright with gems, blazing like fires, the flaming banners of the kings shone forth by the thousand.

sanskrit: mahendraketavaḥ śubhrā mahendrasadaneṣv iva saṃnaddhās teṣu te vīrā dadṛśur yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Bright as the banners of great Indra raised in great Indra's halls; and among them those armored heroes, longing for battle, were beheld.

sanskrit: udyatair āyudhaiś citrās talabaddhāḥ kalāpinaḥ ṛṣabhākṣā manuṣyendrāś camūmukhagatā babhuḥ
english: With weapons raised, splendid, their hand-guards bound, their quivers slung, those bull-eyed lords of men shone forth at the head of their hosts.

sanskrit: śakuniḥ saubalaḥ śalyaḥ saindhavo 'tha jayadrathaḥ vindānuvindāv āvantyau kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ
english: Śakuni the son of Subala, Śalya, the Sindhu king Jayadratha, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja,

sanskrit: śrutāyudhaś ca kāliṅgo jayatsenaś ca pārthivaḥ bṛhadbalaś ca kauśalyaḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ
english: Śrutāyudha the Kaliṅga, the king Jayatsena, Bṛhadbala of Kosala, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas —

sanskrit: daśaite puruṣavyāghrāḥ śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ akṣauhiṇīnāṃ patayo yajvāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ
english: these ten tigers among men, heroes with arms like iron bars, commanders of full divisions, performers of sacrifices with abundant gifts,

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo duryodhanavaśānugāḥ rājāno rājaputrāś ca nītimanto mahābalāḥ
english: these and many other kings and princes, wise in statecraft and of great might, followed in Duryodhana's command.

sanskrit: saṃnaddhāḥ samadṛśyanta sveṣv anīkeṣv avasthitāḥ baddhakṛṣṇājināḥ sarve dhvajino muñjamālinaḥ
english: Armored, they were seen each stationed in his own division, all wearing black antelope skins and bearing banners, girt with garlands of muñja grass —

sanskrit: sṛṣṭā duryodhanasyārthe brahmalokāya dīkṣitāḥ samṛddhā daśa vāhinyaḥ parigṛhya vyavasthitāḥ
english: consecrated, as it were, for Duryodhana's cause and dedicated to the world of Brahmā; ten flourishing divisions stood drawn up and ready.

sanskrit: ekādaśī dhārtarāṣṭrī kauravāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ yatra śāṃtanavo 'graṇīḥ
english: The eleventh, the great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, the mighty Kaurava army, stood before all the troops, with the son of Śaṃtanu at its head.

sanskrit: śvetoṣṇīṣaṃ śvetahayaṃ śvetavarmāṇam acyutam apaśyāma mahārāja bhīṣmaṃ candram ivoditam
english: White-turbaned, with white horses and white armor, unshaken, we beheld Bhīṣma, O great king, like the risen moon.

sanskrit: hematāladhvajaṃ bhīṣmaṃ rājate syandane sthitam śvetābhra iva tīkṣṇāṃśuṃ dadṛśuḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ
english: The Kurus and Pāṇḍavas saw Bhīṣma, his banner a golden palm, standing in his silver chariot like the keen-rayed sun amid a white cloud.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā camūmukhe bhīṣmaṃ samakampanta pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayāś ca maheṣvāsā dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ
english: Beholding Bhīṣma at the head of the host, the Pāṇḍavas trembled, and the mighty bowmen of the Sṛñjayas with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head.

sanskrit: jṛmbhamāṇaṃ mahāsiṃhaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣudramṛgā yathā dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhāḥ sarve samudvivijire muhuḥ
english: As small beasts shrink before a great lion yawning wide, so all those led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna shuddered again and again.

sanskrit: ekādaśaitāḥ śrījuṣṭā vāhinyas tava bhārata pāṇḍavānāṃ tathā sapta mahāpuruṣapālitāḥ
english: These eleven divisions of yours, O Bhārata, were graced with splendor, while the Pāṇḍavas' seven were guarded by mighty men.

sanskrit: unmattamakarāvartau mahāgrāhasamākulau yugānte samupetau dvau dṛśyete sāgarāv iva
english: The two hosts looked like two oceans met together at the end of an age — their whirlpools maddened, teeming with great sea-monsters.

sanskrit: naiva nas tādṛśo rājan dṛṣṭapūrvo na ca śrutaḥ anīkānāṃ sametānāṃ samavāyas tathāvidhaḥ
english: Never before, O king, had we seen or heard of such a gathering of assembled armies as this.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yathā sa bhagavān vyāsaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt tathaiva sahitāḥ sarve samājagmur mahīkṣitaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Even as the blessed Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, had foretold, so did all the lords of earth come together, gathered as one.

sanskrit: maghāviṣayagaḥ somas tad dinaṃ pratyapadyata dīpyamānāś ca saṃpetur divi sapta mahāgrahāḥ
english: On that day the moon stood in the mansion of Maghā, and the seven great planets, blazing, came together in the sky.

sanskrit: dvidhābhūta ivāditya udaye pratyadṛśyata jvalantyā śikhayā bhūyo bhānumān udito divi
english: At its rising the sun seemed cleft in two, and the radiant orb, risen in the heavens, blazed again with a flaming crest.

sanskrit: vavāśire ca dīptāyāṃ diśi gomāyuvāyasāḥ lipsamānāḥ śarīrāṇi māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ
english: And toward the blazing quarter jackals and crows cried out, hungering for the bodies, eaters of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: ahany ahani pārthānāṃ vṛddhaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ bharadvājātmajaś caiva prātar utthāya saṃyatau
english: Day after day the aged Kuru grandsire and the son of Bharadvāja, rising at dawn with controlled minds, would say of the Pārthas —

sanskrit: jayo 'stu pāṇḍuputrāṇām ity ūcatur ariṃdamau yuyudhāte tavārthāya yathā sa samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "Let there be victory to the sons of Pāṇḍu" — thus those two tamers of foes spoke, yet fought for your cause, as the compact had been made.

sanskrit: sarvadharmaviśeṣajñaḥ pitā devavratas tava samānīya mahīpālān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Your father Devavrata, knowing all the niceties of dharma, gathered the kings together and spoke these words:

sanskrit: idaṃ vaḥ kṣatriyā dvāraṃ svargāyāpāvṛtaṃ mahat gacchadhvaṃ tena śakrasya brahmaṇaś ca salokatām
english: "O warriors, here is the great gate to heaven, flung open for you; pass through it to dwell in the world of Śakra and of Brahmā.

sanskrit: eṣa vaḥ śāśvataḥ panthāḥ pūrvaiḥ pūrvatarair gataḥ saṃbhāvayata cātmānam avyagramanaso yudhi
english: This is the eternal path trodden by your forefathers and those before them; honor yourselves in battle with minds undismayed.

sanskrit: nābhāgo hi yayātiś ca māndhātā nahuṣo nṛgaḥ saṃsiddhāḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ gatāḥ karmabhir īdṛśaiḥ
english: For Nābhāga and Yayāti, Māndhātṛ, Nahuṣa, and Nṛga, made perfect by deeds such as these, attained the highest abode.

sanskrit: adharmaḥ kṣatriyasyaiṣa yad vyādhimaraṇaṃ gṛhe yad ājau nidhanaṃ yāti so 'sya dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: It is unrighteousness for a warrior to meet death by sickness in his home; but to fall in battle is his eternal dharma."

sanskrit: evam uktā mahīpālā bhīṣmeṇa bharatarṣabha niryayuḥ svāny anīkāni śobhayanto rathottamaiḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bhīṣma, O bull of the Bharatas, the kings marched forth, gracing their own divisions with their splendid chariots.

sanskrit: sa tu vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ sāmātyaḥ saha bandhubhiḥ nyāsitaḥ samare śastraṃ bhīṣmeṇa bharatarṣabha
english: But that Karṇa, son of the Sun, with his counselors and kinsmen, was made by Bhīṣma to lay down his weapons in the battle, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: apetakarṇāḥ putrās te rājānaś caiva tāvakāḥ niryayuḥ siṃhanādena nādayanto diśo daśa
english: Then your sons and the kings on your side, now without Karṇa, marched forth, making the ten quarters resound with their lion-roars.

sanskrit: śvetaiś chatraiḥ patākābhir dhvajavāraṇavājibhiḥ tāny anīkāny aśobhanta rathair atha padātibhiḥ
english: With white parasols and pennons, with banners, elephants, and horses, with chariots and foot soldiers, those divisions shone in splendor.

sanskrit: bherīpaṇavaśabdaiś ca paṭahānāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ rathanemininādaiś ca babhūvākulitā mahī
english: With the sound of drums and tabors and the din of war-drums, and with the rumble of chariot wheels, the earth was set atremble.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadakeyūraiḥ kārmukaiś ca mahārathāḥ bhrājamānā vyadṛśyanta jaṅgamāḥ parvatā iva
english: With golden armlets and bracelets and with their bows, the great chariot-warriors were seen gleaming like moving mountains.

sanskrit: tālena mahatā bhīṣmaḥ pañcatāreṇa ketunā vimalādityasaṃkāśas tasthau kurucamūpatiḥ
english: Bhīṣma, the lord of the Kuru host, bearing as his standard a great palm-tree with five stars, stood there like the spotless sun.

sanskrit: ye tvadīyā maheṣvāsā rājāno bharatarṣabha avartanta yathādeśaṃ rājañ śāṃtanavasya te
english: Those mighty bowmen, the kings of your side, O bull of the Bharatas, moved according to the command of the son of Śaṃtanu, O king.

sanskrit: sa tu govāsanaḥ śaibyaḥ sahitaḥ sarvarājabhiḥ yayau mātaṅgarājena rājārheṇa patākinā padmavarṇas tv anīkānāṃ sarveṣām agrataḥ sthitaḥ
english: And the Śaibya king Govāsana, with all his royal allies, advanced upon a kingly, pennoned lordly elephant; lotus-hued, he stood at the very front of all the divisions.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā yayau yattaḥ siṃhalāṅgūlaketanaḥ śrutāyuś citrasenaś ca purumitro viviṃśatiḥ
english: Aśvatthāman marched out, intent, his banner bearing a lion's tail; and Śrutāyu, Citrasena, Purumitra, and Viviṃśati,

sanskrit: śalyo bhūriśravāś caiva vikarṇaś ca mahārathaḥ ete sapta maheṣvāsā droṇaputrapurogamāḥ syandanair varavarṇābhair bhīṣmasyāsan puraḥsarāḥ
english: Śalya, Bhūriśravas, and Vikarṇa the great chariot-warrior — these seven mighty bowmen, led by Droṇa's son, with their chariots of splendid hue, formed Bhīṣma's vanguard.

sanskrit: teṣām api mahotsedhāḥ śobhayanto rathottamān bhrājamānā vyadṛśyanta jāmbūnadamayā dhvajāḥ
english: Their banners too, lofty and wrought of gold, gracing those splendid chariots, were seen shining bright.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayī vediḥ kamaṇḍaluvibhūṣitā ketur ācāryamukhyasya droṇasya dhanuṣā saha
english: A golden altar adorned with a water-pot, together with a bow, was the standard of Droṇa, foremost of teachers.

sanskrit: anekaśatasāhasram anīkam anukarṣataḥ mahān duryodhanasyāsīn nāgo maṇimayo dhvajaḥ
english: Drawing along a host of many hundreds of thousands, Duryodhana's great standard was an elephant fashioned of jewels.

sanskrit: tasya pauravakāliṅgau kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣemadhanvā sumitraś ca tasthuḥ pramukhato rathāḥ
english: Before him stood, in their chariots, Paurava and the Kaliṅga king, Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, Kṣemadhanvan, and Sumitrā.

sanskrit: syandanena mahārheṇa ketunā vṛṣabheṇa ca prakarṣann iva senāgraṃ māgadhaś ca nṛpo yayau
english: And the king of Magadha marched forth in a costly chariot, his standard a bull, as though drawing the army's van after him.

sanskrit: tad aṅgapatinā guptaṃ kṛpeṇa ca mahātmanā śāradābhracayaprakhyaṃ prācyānām abhavad balam
english: Guarded by the lord of the Aṅgas and by the great-souled Kṛpa, the host of the easterners looked like a mass of autumn clouds.

sanskrit: anīkapramukhe tiṣṭhan varāheṇa mahāyaśāḥ śuśubhe ketumukhyena rājatena jayadrathaḥ
english: Standing at the head of his division, the illustrious Jayadratha shone with his foremost standard, a silver boar.

sanskrit: śataṃ rathasahasrāṇāṃ tasyāsan vaśavartinaḥ aṣṭau nāgasahasrāṇi sādinām ayutāni ṣaṭ
english: A hundred thousand chariots obeyed his command, eight thousand elephants, and sixty thousand horsemen.

sanskrit: tat sindhupatinā rājan pālitaṃ dhvajinīmukham anantarathanāgāśvam aśobhata mahad balam
english: That vanguard of the army, guarded by the lord of the Sindhus, O king — a great force with chariots, elephants, and horses past counting — shone in splendor.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭyā rathasahasrais tu nāgānām ayutena ca patiḥ sarvakaliṅgānāṃ yayau ketumatā saha
english: With sixty thousand chariots and ten thousand elephants, the lord of all the Kaliṅgas marched forth, together with Ketumat.

sanskrit: tasya parvatasaṃkāśā vyarocanta mahāgajāḥ yantratomaratūṇīraiḥ patākābhiś ca śobhitāḥ
english: His great elephants, like mountains, shone forth, adorned with engines, lances, and quivers, and with pennons.

sanskrit: śuśubhe ketumukhyena pādapena kaliṅgapaḥ śvetacchatreṇa niṣkeṇa cāmaravyajanena ca
english: The Kaliṅga king shone with his foremost standard of a tree, with his white parasol, his golden ornament, and his yak-tail fan.

sanskrit: ketumān api mātaṅgaṃ vicitraparamāṅkuśam āsthitaḥ samare rājan meghastha iva bhānumān
english: Ketumat too, mounted in battle upon an elephant with a wondrously fine goad, O king, was like the sun set within a cloud.

sanskrit: tejasā dīpyamānas tu vāraṇottamam āsthitaḥ bhagadatto yayau rājā yathā vajradharas tathā
english: Blazing with splendor, mounted upon a noble elephant, King Bhagadatta marched forth like the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: gajaskandhagatāv āstāṃ bhagadattena saṃmitau vindānuvindāv āvantyau ketumantam anuvratau
english: Riding upon the shoulders of elephants, the equals of Bhagadatta, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti followed in Ketumat's train.

sanskrit: sa rathānīkavān vyūho hastyaṅgottamaśīrṣavān vājipakṣaḥ patann ugraḥ prāharat sarvatomukhaḥ
english: That formation, rich in chariot-troops, with elephant-bodies and a noble head, with cavalry for wings, descended fierce and struck out, facing every way.

sanskrit: droṇena vihito rājan rājñā śāṃtanavena ca tathaivācāryaputreṇa bāhlīkena kṛpeṇa ca
english: It was ordered, O king, by Droṇa and by the royal son of Śaṃtanu, and likewise by the teacher's son, by Bāhlīka, and by Kṛpa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato muhūrtāt tumulaḥ śabdo hṛdayakampanaḥ aśrūyata mahārāja yodhānāṃ prayuyutsatām
english: Saṃjaya said: Then in a moment, O great king, a tumultuous, heart-shaking din was heard from the warriors eager to fight.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣair vāraṇānāṃ ca bṛṃhitaiḥ rathānāṃ nemighoṣaiś ca dīryatīva vasuṃdharā
english: With the blare of conches and kettledrums, with the trumpeting of elephants, and with the rumble of chariot wheels, the earth itself seemed to split apart.
